chapter: Cafe Society and the Zodiac Suite
title: Hal Baker goes to Ellington and her band falls apart
summary: Her husband Harold Baker left overnight with Ellington. She tried Pittsburgh replacements and Kelly's Stable in New York but disbanded, while Fletcher Henderson hired Blakey's Pittsburghers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I didn't see him. They had a meeting of the musicians and I didn't know about it. All I did was take care of the music and play. So I waited for him. We had a couple more days to go. We didn't have no trumpet player. I was really disgusted to discover that he had left with Duke Ellington's band. Now, I'm the leader of the band and I don't even know what was going on. So later on when I heard from him I discovered that the boys got in great arguments and whatnot when he wasn't home with me. He was trying to break up their arguments. They were jealous and some of them wanted all Pittsburghers in the band and didn't want anyone from St. Louis, and a lot of foolish things were happening that I didn't know about. So when Duke Ellington heard Hal Baker he hired him right on the spot and he left the next day.

With the group and after that these kids that wanted all Pittsburghers - Art Blakey said to me, "Well, it's good he's gone because there's a guy in Pittsburgh that's the greatest." I said, "O.K., we'll go by and pick him up." We had another engagement, I think through John Hammond, Kelly's Stable in New York with Thelma Carpenter, a great singer. What happened, they brought in a guy from Pittsburgh and the boy couldn't even play the parts. See, Hal Baker was so terrific and he'd take about 10 choruses.

He'd jump back on the ensembles with the group. I just never could find another trumpet player to play as good as Harold did. We tried out several musicians. We tried out everybody but Dizzy Gillespie and he wasn't around then, you know. So when we came to New York I decided to dis-band and not even bother because the other kid wasn't good enough for the group. So I didn't hear from Harold for quite a while and I stayed in Kelly's Stable I think for about 4 weeks and I decided to come out. I don't know where Art Blakey went and his group but I heard later that Fletcher Henderson went to Pittsburgh and hired all Pittsburghers with Art Blakey and they got angry with him when he was on his way to Chicago and when he reached the job where he was going, he had no band! So I was kind of glad to get out of that.
